name: DNP-enhanced magic-angle-spinning solid-state NMR of an amorphous drug at 100 K, 9.39 T and 264 GHz microwave irradiation
plain_name: Boost a magnetic resonance signal by cooling a drug powder to 100 K
description: An amorphous PROTAC drug substance is impregnated with a 12 mM AMUPol radical solution, packed into a 3.2 mm sapphire rotor and measured by dynamic-nuclear-polarisation solid-state NMR at 9.39 T with the sample at 100 K, 10 kHz magic-angle spinning and 264 GHz microwave irradiation from a klystron. The low temperature is what makes the DNP signal enhancement, and hence natural-abundance structure determination of the amorphous drug, possible.
keywords: Boost a magnetic resonance signal by cooling a drug powder to 100 K

sources.citation: D. Torodii, J. B. Holmes, M. Cordova, et al., Determination of key functional structures of an amorphous VHL-based SMARCA2 PROTAC, Nature Communications 16:9694 (2025)

H. Karlsson, A. C. Pinon, L. Karlson, et al., Position-Specific Substitution in Cellulose Ethers Studied by DNP Enhanced Solid-State NMR Spectroscopy, Magnetic Resonance in Chemistry 63(8):560-568 (2025) - second procedure on a pharmaceutical excipient (400 MHz Bruker Ascend DNP magnet, 263 GHz gyrotron, ~104 K, 3.2 mm LTMAS)

reported_equipment: 263-GHz gyrotron and a 3.2-mm LTMAS DNP probe

requirements.rationale: The DNP experiments are run with the sample temperature set to 100 K.
DNP enhancement requires the sample to be cooled to about 100 K; a machine limited to higher temperatures gives no usable enhancement.
The spectrometer operates at 9.39 T (9390 mT); the cold sample space must sit inside a magnet of at least that field.
The sample is packed in a 3.2 mm (3200 um) outer-diameter sapphire rotor, which must fit the machine's cold sample space.
Polarisation transfer needs 264 GHz microwaves delivered to the cold sample through a corrugated waveguide, so the machine must pass that frequency into the sample space.

confirmation_note: Requirements taken from the cited procedure and independently re-verified against the source (research/v4, 2026-11-01). Users must confirm them for their own run; edits require confirmation again.
